features.name: Fwd Seg Size Min
features.description: Minimum forward segment size in bytes, reflecting smallest payload segment observed.
features.implication: Minimum forward segment size; interpret together with payload length and rate.

features.name: RST Flag Cnt
features.description: Total count of packets with the TCP RST flag set in both directions.
features.implication: Elevated RST count can indicate aborted or refused connections during active sessions.

features.name: Init Fwd Win Byts
features.description: Initial TCP window bytes in forward direction; typically -1 when unrecorded.
features.implication: Anomalous or absent forward window values can flag scanning or attack tools.

features.name: Tot Fwd Pkts
features.description: Total number of packets transmitted in the forward direction from source to destination.
features.implication: High forward packet counts with few backward packets are consistent with one-sided flooding.

features.name: Tot Bwd Pkts
features.description: Total number of packets transmitted in the backward direction from destination to source.
features.implication: Near-zero backward packet count is consistent with unanswered DoS flooding traffic.

Direct Network Flood s are when one or more systems are used to send a high-volume of network packets towards the targeted service's network. Almost any network protocol may be used for flooding. Stateless protocols such as UDP or ICMP are commonly used but stateful protocols such as TCP can be used as well. Botnets are commonly used to conduct network flooding attacks against networks and services. Large botnets can generate a significant amount of traffic from systems spread across the global Internet. To perform Network DoS attacks several aspects apply to multiple methods, including IP address spoofing, and botnets. Adversaries may use the original IP address of an attacking system, or spoof the source IP address to make the attack traffic more difficult to trace back to the attacking system or to enable reflection.
